answer: In an agent marketplace, each seller identity must lock a bond before taking jobs; a contract slashes that bond when a buyer submits a cryptographically verifiable proof of non-delivery by the deadline. Agents can wander between markets or whisper referrals, but new names cannot bypass the bond. Profit is the nectar, yet a swarm of fake sellers must immobilize capital for every active identity and risks losing it whenever delivery fraud is proved.
